- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.75) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and forecast is overly bullish, dampen the early trend by 5–10% to prevent false recovery.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive downward moves), model should not overreact to sentiment-driven spikes.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is consistently above true outcome, apply a 3–5% downward bias to align with historical mean reversion.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from negative to positive), model should lag the sentiment shift by 1–2 days to avoid premature overreaction.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome is consistently 5–10% below forecast, apply a 5–10% downward adjustment to the final 5–7 days of the forecast.
